lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: classifying two-dimensional figures and identifying lines of symmetry
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: classifying two-dimensional figures and identifying lines of symmetry

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

items.prompt: A triangle where one angle measures more than 90° is called what kind of triangle?

steps: One angle over 90° makes it an obtuse triangle.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
Which term describes two lines in the same plane that never meet and stay the same distance apart?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A triangle where all three angles measure less than 90° is called what kind of triangle?
How many lines of symmetry does a equilateral triangle have?
Which term describes a part of a line that has one endpoint and extends forever in one direction?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A triangle where all three sides are the same length is called what kind of triangle?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
